conclusion: Dominant measured preflight delay precedes completion of inspection and/or occurs in lifecycle checking; post-inspection caller resumption is below 0.009ms per-request aggregate, also on failures. This excludes long post-inspection continuation delay in this run, not internal continuation scheduling, filesystem completion delay, or their combination. No provider queue or lock-availability wait exists in this SQLite path. Lifecycle duration is elapsed time around a single asynchronous marker lstat with existing rejection recovery, not time waiting for a held lock.
limitations: Provider-owned completion is not a direct Promise settlement timestamp. No CPU, disk-latency, libuv-threadpool, OS-scheduling or GC attribution.

Inspection includes safeRoot sequential ancestor lstats, realpath, database and sidecar lstats, and their internal continuations. Lifecycle includes lstat, existing catch reaction, and both continuations.
Inspection preflightToResume nests operation and continuation; full sqlitePreflight includes inspection and lifecycle. Do not add nested spans or infer CPU by subtraction.
One host and three repetitions. No inference of statistical benefit or universal concurrency threshold. All sampler tails are incomplete; pending callback lateness is only a lower bound.
Only the largest operation tuple is retained per request; sum intervals do not pair with individual calls beyond the bounded tuple. Existing ledger checkpoints bracket larger service intervals.

counterExperiment.reason: Primary measurement already excludes large post-inspection resumption delay. Resolving filesystem completion versus internal scheduling requires a different completion boundary; preserve that as the next bounded investigation instead of another load run.

nextExperiment: Observe the existing lifecycle lstat ENOENT recovery callback before it returns null, and resumption of the awaiting lifecycle function, without adding a Promise reaction. This distinguishes recovery-to-continuation delay inside the long lifecycle interval; raw filesystem completion remains unobserved.
